entries.title: Player Data Export
entries.summary: Export/import JSON backup of characters and parties from the home screen.
entries.body:
Use Export Player Data on the home screen to download characters and parties as JSON.

Import restores roster entries on the same or a new server.

Sessions are not included — back up appdata game.db for full save-game archive.

Icon SVG files must be in the Docker image (git). Custom icon assignments sync via icons.json; generated fallback entries for room states, classes, and monsters are recreated by the API.

entries.title: Saved Games
entries.summary: Sessions auto-save to server SQLite; explicit Save pins a game in the list.
entries.body:
Every action updates the server session in game.db (appdata volume).

Save Game marks the session in Saved Games for easy reload. You may enter an optional **save label** (e.g. "Floor 3 — boss room"); labels appear in Active and Saved Games lists instead of the default party + adventure title.

The browser stores only the active session id — refresh reloads from the server.

Camp/retreat keeps the dungeon but does not write roster rewards until a clean complete exit.

While camped or from a saved game, use Regroup Party to swap heroes (see Camp Outside).

entries.title: Home Character Sheets
entries.summary: Roster sheets show home-bank gold, banked XP rolls, stored gear, rules notes, and spending actions.
entries.body:
On the home screen, click a roster hero to expand their character sheet.

The sheet shows Home bank gold, Banked XP rolls, Clues, carry limits, stored gear, spells, and a Rules & abilities reference section for class notes and learned tier skills.

Rules & abilities is a nested details control inside the selected roster row; opening it does not collapse the selected hero.

Banked XP spending is available from the expanded home sheet when the hero is not locked in an active adventure. If the hero is adventuring, spend banked XP from the party sheet instead.

Stored gear is the between-adventure item store. The app does not maintain a second item-bank account; roster inventory is the stored gear model.

entries.title: Tier Dice
entries.summary: Tier training unlocks action dice: Basic d6, Expert d8, Heroic d10, Legendary d12, Epic d20.
entries.body:
Expanded Edition tier dice apply to PC Attack, Defense, Save, and spellcasting rolls after the matching tier has been entered.

Tier 1 Basic: d6, explodes on 6.
Tier 2 Expert: d8, explodes on 7–8.
Tier 3 Heroic: d10, explodes on 8+.
Tier 4 Legendary: d12, explodes on 9+.
Tier 5 Epic: d20, explodes on 10+.

Expert tier advancement rolls (Classical / Slower) use d8+2 per Four Against the Abyss, but only after Expert tier training has been recorded.

entries.title: Tier Training
entries.summary: Between adventures, pay gold and/or banked XP to record Expert, Heroic, or Legendary tier training.
entries.body:
Forsaken Depths tier entry (summary p.9) gates advancement into higher tiers. Use Tier training on the party sheet between adventures.

Expert tier entry costs 500gp from the party or 1 banked XP roll instead of gold. This unlocks Expert advancement, Expert dice, and the option to learn Expert skills/spells later; it does not itself buy an Expert skill.

Exact gold and banked-XP costs are in tier_training_costs_table (Rules tables panel).

entries.title: Heroic Skills (Four Against the Abyss)
entries.source: Four Against the Abyss heroic tier
entries.summary: L10+ heroes may learn heroic skills via the XP fork after Heroic tier training; all 45 heroic skills wired.
entries.body:
After Heroic tier training (Forsaken Depths p.9), classical or slower XP advancement at L10+ may be spent to learn one heroic skill instead of gaining +1 Level.

The full catalog is in heroic_skills_table on the home Rules tables panel (mechanic and wired status columns). **All 45 heroic skills are wired** in combat, exploration, reactions, rest, traps, and crafting flows.

Declare Aggressive/Defensive Stance, Master Strike, Double Shot, Mass Blessing, Ward of Protection, and Restore in the Combat Focus hero drawer before Fight Round. Bank Training Focus and use Restore Mental Capacity from the party sheet in exploration.

Song of Elidra applies to one reaction check per adventure and can be heard by heroes on the same or an adjacent connected map element, including split-party/scout situations; Legendary Song raises the bonus.

Legendary upgrades require the matching heroic skill first.

entries.title: Legendary Skills (Four Against the Abyss)
entries.source: Four Against the Abyss legendary tier
entries.summary: L15+ heroes may learn legendary skills via the XP fork after Legendary tier training; all 20 legendary upgrades wired.
entries.body:
After Legendary tier training, classical or slower XP advancement at L15+ may be spent to learn one legendary skill instead of gaining +1 Level.

Each legendary skill upgrades a specific heroic skill — see legendary_skills_table and the upgrades column on heroic_skills_table. **All 20 legendary upgrades are wired**, including Beast Leadership, Climber, Memory, Song of Elidra, Swimmer, and Ward of Protection.

entries.title: Expert Skills (Four Against the Abyss)
entries.summary: All Abyss expert skills are wired; Expert-trained L5+ heroes may spend one advancement XP roll to learn a skill instead of gaining a level.
entries.body:
Four Against the Abyss (pp.14–23): after a hero has entered Expert tier, a successful advancement roll may be spent to learn one expert skill instead of gaining +1 Level.

Expert tier entry is separate: pay 500gp or 1 banked XP roll through Tier training first. The later skill-learning attempt spends one advancement XP roll and does not require an extra tier-entry payment.

Roll the tier advancement die with the Forsaken Depths modifier (Expert d8+2, Heroic d10+4, …). Success if the total exceeds current Level, or the natural die shows the high auto-success faces.

Each skill is normally taken once per hero. Impervious may be learned again for a new monster type; Sworn Enemy and Impervious require choosing a foe keyword when learned.

All expert skills in expert_skills_table are implemented in play, including combat skills (Whirlwind of Steel, Shield Bash, Combat Acrobatics, Dying Action, Knife Throwing), exploration (Acute Hearing listen-at-door, Super Logic puzzle bonus), between-adventure crafting (Scroll Maker, Create Holy Water, Arcane Tanner), and utility (Continual Light, Lesser Necromancy, Spore Alchemy).

See expert_skill_implementation_table on the home Rules tables panel for per-skill mechanics.

Tier training between adventures (Expert / Heroic / Legendary gates) is summarized under Tier Training; costs are in tier_training_costs_table.

entries.title: Between Adventures
entries.summary: Full heal on clean exit; buy gear; refresh spell lists.
entries.body:
After a completed adventure, surviving heroes fully heal.

Buy or sell equipment at home (p.16 / p.19). Roster gold is home bank gold and is uncapped outside the dungeon.

Casters prepare spells before the next delve; once-per-adventure abilities refresh.

Each hero may only be in one active adventure at a time in this app.

entries.title: Equipment Shop
entries.summary: Buy gear between adventures; sell loot by p.19 resale rules.
entries.body:
Home equipment shop (p.16): buy weapons, armor, shields, and gear before or between adventures. Use the Quantity field for repeated purchases such as 5x Bandage; the app checks the total price before buying.

While camped outside an active dungeon, living party members may also use the Equipment Shop before re-entering. Purchases spend from the hero's carried gold plus home-bank gold; the 200gp carried-gold limit applies only inside the dungeon.

Potion of Healing normally uses the shop price, but a party with Recipe for a Potion unlocks the 50gp potion price.

Sell items at half list price. Magic equipment may be sold but not bought (p.19); fixed magic resale values are listed in equipment_shop_table. Someone Will Pay Big Money for That triples one gem/jewel/jewelry sale and consumes that Secret.

Class restrictions apply — the shop hides or blocks forbidden items.

entries.title: Barbarian — Rage Attack
entries.summary: 1 + level÷2 rage attacks per adventure; roll 3d6 keep best; double damage on hit.
entries.body:
Barbarians add +L to melee and ranged Attack rolls.

Rage attacks per adventure: 1 + 1 for each 2 full levels (2 at L2, 3 at L4, etc.).

When performing a rage attack, roll the d6 three times and choose the best result, then add modifiers. If the rage attack hits, it inflicts double damage.

Barbarians may not use magic items, scrolls, or potions (may carry for allies). They accept divine healing from clerics and may use holy water.

Illiterate — cannot gain Clues from inscriptions.

entries.title: Cleric
entries.summary: +½L Attack, +L vs undead; Healing and Blessing prayers.
entries.body:
Clerics add +½L Attack (+L vs undead) and cast divine prayers.

Healing: 3× per adventure, d6+L Life. Blessing: removes qualifying conditions.

Light or heavy armor with shield. Life: 4+L. Starting wealth d6gp.

Stealth +½L.

entries.title: Expert Spells (Four Against the Abyss)
entries.summary: Expert-trained L5+ wizard/elf heroes may learn expert spells through the Expert skill XP fork; all six Abyss cast effects are wired.
entries.body:
Four Against the Abyss (pp.24–25): Expert-trained wizards and elves at Level 5+ may learn expert spells using the same advancement fork as expert skills. The spell is added to the hero's repertoire and appears on the party sheet.

Expert tier entry is paid first through Tier training. The spell-learning attempt later spends one advancement XP roll instead of gaining a level.

Learning and casting are implemented for Healing Surge, Infallible Missile, Lifeforce Control, Mass Teleport, Aura of Terror, and Reverse Gaze.

**Lifeforce Control** and **Mass Teleport** work in combat or exploration: choose Life to transfer, teleport destination (visited rooms), and which allies move (Mass Teleport costs the caster 1 Life per ally moved). See expert_spells_table in the Rules tables panel for mechanics and class eligibility.

entries.title: Food Rations
entries.summary: Halflings start with extra rations; Nourishing Meal spends 1 per eater when resting.
entries.body:
Food rations are consumed by Halfling Nourishing Meal when resting (1 ration per ally who eats).

Rangers and halflings often start with rations from class starting gear.

Track rations on hero inventory; short supplies limit who can eat the meal.

entries.title: Consumables — Oil, Acid, Mushrooms
entries.summary: Lantern oil and acid vials in combat; rare mushrooms eaten in exploration.
entries.body:
**Lantern oil (extra light):** Buy at the home equipment shop (8gp) or find in caverns/fungal grottoes. Combat only — splash on a **regenerating** foe (party sheet). Hit inflicts 1 Life and blocks troll regeneration that round; counts as attacking.

**Acid vial:** Buy at the home shop (30gp). Combat only — throw at any foe (party sheet). Acid damage blocks regeneration like other acid sources.

**Rare mushrooms (EE p.159):** From the fungal grottoes treasure sub-table. Eat during exploration via party sheet: healing (+1 Life), strength (+1 Attack next fight), clarity (+1 next spell roll), poison (blade poison), madness (Fear Save vs L3), or golden (3d6×10gp).

entries.title: Halfling — Luck
entries.summary: L+1 Luck points per adventure; spend 1 to reroll or flee without parting blows.
entries.body:
Halflings add +L Defense vs giants, trolls, ogres, and half-giants, and +L to sling attacks.

Luck points per adventure: L+1.

Spend 1 Luck point to:
• Run away from melee without receiving a parting attack (whole party escapes cleanly when declared at flee).
• Reroll an Attack or Defense roll (combat Ability dropdown).
• Reroll a Save (party-sheet button after a failed save prompt).
• Reroll Search on the current tile after searching (party-sheet **Luck: reroll search**).
• Reroll Treasure on the current tile after a treasure roll (**Luck: reroll treasure**).

Luck replenishes between adventures. Gaining or losing a level immediately adjusts Luck points by 1.

entries.title: Halfling — Nourishing Meal
entries.summary: Once per adventure when resting; 1 Food ration per ally eating; +1 Life each.
entries.body:
Once per adventure when Resting, a halfling may cook a Nourishing Meal using 1 Food ration per ally who eats.

Each ally eating heals +1 Life in addition to normal rest recovery. Halflings eating also recover 1 Madness.

If rations are short, only some allies may eat.

entries.title: Rogue
entries.summary: +L Defense and vs outnumbered minors; +L on traps and lockpick.
entries.body:
Rogues add +L Defense and +L Attack vs minor foes when the party outnumbers them.

+L to Saves vs traps and lockpick attempts.

Light armor only. Life: 3+L. Stealth +L.

A rogue in marching-order position 1 or 2 may detect and disarm a trap before it goes off.

entries.title: Warrior
entries.summary: +L Attack with any melee or ranged weapon; any armor; Life 6+L.
entries.body:
Warriors add +L to all Attack rolls.

Any armor and weapons allowed. Scroll use as L1 caster.

Life: 6+L. Starting wealth 2d6gp.

Can bash locked doors. Advanced skills from Level 5+.

entries.title: Wizard
entries.summary: L+2 spell slots; +L spellcasting; no armor.
entries.body:
Wizards add +L to spellcasting. L+2 prepared slots per adventure.

Copy spells from scrolls; burn spellbook pages as emergency scrolls.

No armor. Life: 2+L. Starting wealth 4d6gp.

+L Saves vs puzzles and magic.

entries.title: Dungeon Entrance
entries.summary: The outside door stands open behind you; your first inner door opens without a roll.
entries.body:
When the adventure begins, the party is already inside the entrance map element. The dungeon exit (outside door) you came through stands open behind you.

To explore deeper, choose any unexplored exit from the entrance. The first time you pass through an inner entrance door, it opens automatically — no Door Table roll.

When you backtrack to the entrance, inner doors you opened stay open (rulebook p.25).

entries.title: Dwarf
entries.summary: +L melee; gold sense before fight; greedy gold split; no bribes with 2+ dwarves.
entries.body:
Dwarves add +L to melee Attack (+1 vs goblins; +1 Defense vs giants, ogres, trolls).

Gold Sense: Save vs L6 (+L) when meeting foes to preview treasure roll.

Greedy: each dwarf must receive at least 1gp from any gold find.

Miser: parties with 2+ dwarves cannot bribe foes. +20% resale on gems and jewelry.

entries.title: Elf
entries.summary: L spell slots; +L melee/ranged except two-handed; +1 vs orcs.
entries.body:
Elves add +L to melee and ranged Attack except with two-handed melee weapons. +1 vs orcs and orc-kind.

L spell slots from wizard basics (except Blessing). +L to spellcasting.

Light armor only when casting; shield may be slung on back (1 turn to ready). Life: 4+L.

entries.title: Ranger
entries.summary: +L Attack; dual melee at ½L each; outdoors bow twice at ½L each.
entries.body:
Rangers add +L to Attack.

Two matching melee weapons: attack once per weapon at +½L each (no exploding dice on those attacks).

Outdoors: bow twice per turn at +½L each (no exploding dice).

May learn one druid spell from a scroll with XP roll. Life: 6+L.

entries.title: Druid
entries.summary: 2+L druid slots; wilderness animal companion (wolf/bear/panther); expert spells from quests or Clues.
entries.body:
Druids add +½L Attack. 2+L spell slots, +L spellcasting.

**Animal companion (EE p.32):** On entering a wilderness tile, a druid with a Food ration may welcome a wolf (L3, 4 Life), bear (L4, 6 Life), or panther (L3, 3 Life). The companion attacks for 1 Life each round and draws foe attacks; if slain the druid gains 1 Madness. Offer another Food ration when returning to wilderness to replace it.

**Call of the Wild (EE p.38):** Level 10+ druids may leave the party for d6 turns to commune with nature. While away, the druid is detached and cannot navigate, fight, cast, trigger detached wandering fights, or rejoin. Dungeon-time actions count the duration down; when it reaches 0, the druid can rejoin from the party sheet.

Expert spells via quest reward, 3 Clues, XP roll, or expert scroll (consumes scroll).

Life: 3+L. Light armor, leafsteel, shield.

entries.title: Druid — Call of the Wild
entries.summary: At Level 10+, a druid may leave the party for d6 turns to commune with nature.
entries.body:
Use Call of the Wild from the Level 10+ druid's party sheet during exploration.

The app rolls d6 turns and detaches the druid on the current map element. While the countdown is above 0, that druid cannot act, fight, cast, navigate as a detached group, trigger detached wandering fights, or rejoin.

Dungeon-time actions such as movement, searching, combat rounds, rest, door actions, trap resolution, weapon swaps, and detached combat rounds reduce the countdown. When it reaches 0, the party sheet enables Rejoin main group.

entries.title: Illusionist
entries.summary: L+3 illusion slots; distracting lights; continual light item.
entries.body:
Illusionists add +L spellcasting. L+3 slots for illusion-list spells.

Distracting lights reduce foe Level by Tier (1 turn, once per foe per fight).

Continual light on worn item. Illusionary knife throw uses slot for +Tier +L attack.

No armor. Life: 2+L.

entries.title: Swashbuckler
entries.summary: +½L Attack and Defense; two attacks with hand plus off-hand light weapon.
entries.body:
Swashbucklers add +½L to Attack and Defense.

Each turn: one attack with a hand weapon and one with an off-hand light weapon.

Panache: gain 1 point per kill (max L); spend 1 for +1 on next Attack or Defense.

Life: 4+L. Light armor. See Panache entry for spend rules.

entries.title: Swashbuckler — Panache
entries.summary: Gain Panache up to L from kills; spend 1 for +1 on next Attack or Defense.
entries.body:
Swashbucklers add +½L to Attack and Defense and may make two attacks per turn (hand weapon + off-hand light weapon).

Panache: gain 1 point per foe slain, up to a maximum of L.

Spend 1 Panache to add +1 to the next Attack or Defense roll (maximum 1 point per roll).

entries.title: Paladin
entries.summary: +L Attack; prayer points; auto-resist Fear; strict mission rules.
entries.body:
Paladins add +L Attack, heavy armor, and Blessing prayer.

Prayer points (L+1): heal Life, reroll Saves, summon outdoor steed.

Auto-succeed Fear Saves. Pay L×10gp tithe after each adventure.

Will not abandon a mission while foes remain; special withdrawal rules when the party is badly hurt.

entries.title: Paladin — Prayer Points
entries.summary: L+1 prayer points; heal Life, reroll failed Saves, or summon an outdoor steed.
entries.body:
Paladins add +L to Attack rolls.

Prayer points per adventure: L+1. Spend points on:

1. Heal 1 Life on yourself or an ally (any number of points at a time in the rules; the app spends one point per click).
2. Reroll a failed Save.
3. Summon a steed for one day outdoors (not in combat; not in demonic planes).

The party sheet shows a Prayer heal target selector for living allies/self and disables the heal button when nobody is wounded.

A mounted paladin who is not surprised attacks non-mounted foes at +1.

Paladins pay L×10gp tithe after adventures and have special withdrawal restrictions. Auto-succeed Fear Saves.

entries.title: Acrobat — Tricks
entries.summary: L+3 Trick points; evade flee, distract foes, unarmed attacks.
entries.body:
Acrobats add +½L Attack and +L Defense.

L+3 Trick points per adventure; recover Tier tricks when Resting.

Tricks include: Leap out of Harm (reroll non-magical Save), Shift Position (swap marching order), Distract (−Tier foe Level), Flip Kick / Double Kick (unarmed), Evade (leave melee without attack), Serpent Twist (escape grabs), Knife Throw (+Tier).

Life: 3+L.

entries.title: Assassin
entries.summary: Hide in shadows for triple damage on marked living target next turn.
entries.body:
Assassins add +L Attack with all weapons.

Hide in Shadows: Stealth Save (+L) vs foe Level. On success, next attack vs marked target triples damage on a hit (living anatomy only until L4 XP unlock).

Only one assassin may hide at a time. Light armor. Life: 3+L.

entries.title: Bulwark
entries.summary: Rare tank; +½L melee Defense; others must be healed before bulwark except at 1 Life.
entries.body:
Only one bulwark per party. +½L melee Attack, +½L Defense, +Tier ranged Attack.

Other heroes must be fully healed before magical healing applies to the bulwark unless the bulwark is at 1 Life.

Heavy armor, shield. Life: 7+L. Expert Sacrifice Defense may intercept ally damage.

entries.title: Camp Outside the Dungeon
entries.summary: Exit with fallen heroes inside to camp; dungeon state persists for a rescue run.
entries.body:
If any hero remains fallen inside when the party uses the dungeon exit, the party camps outside instead of completing the adventure.

The explored dungeon, bodies, and tile state persist. Re-enter through any previously connected exit from the entrance.

Unattended bodies may lose gear to theft on retreat (5-in-6 per item).

Deliver a carried body at the exit to trigger recovery options.

The Camp Outside panel is the between-forays hub for the linked party + dungeon: Return to Dungeon, Bank, Transfer, Equipment Shop, Regroup Party, or Abandon Dungeon.

While camped outside, the home bank is available from the Camp panel and the Home Screen Bank button: deposit carried gold before re-entering, deposit all party carried gold, or withdraw up to the 200gp carried-gold cap. On the home screen, the Bank button shows a stop-style unavailable state when the current active session is not camped outside.

While camped (or from a saved game), you may regroup — swap party members before re-entering. Fallen heroes remain on their tiles even if replaced on the roster.

entries.title: Carrying Fallen Heroes
entries.summary: Rear-guard hero may carry one body; carrier is auto-hit in combat.
entries.body:
A living hero in the rearguard (#3–#4) may carry one fallen comrade's body.

The carrier suffers automatic hits from foes while hauling the body.

Deliver the body at the dungeon exit for resurrection or recovery options.

Gear stays on the body until redistributed.

entries.title: Fallen Heroes and Recovery
entries.summary: Carry bodies to the entrance; camp outside to persist the dungeon; 1000gp resurrection.
entries.body:
Heroes at 0 Life fall on the current tile. Their gear remains on the body.

A survivor in the rearguard may carry one body (foes auto-hit the carrier).

Deliver a carried body at the dungeon exit for recovery options.

If any hero remains fallen inside when the party exits, the party camps outside — the explored dungeon persists for a rescue run. Unattended bodies may lose gear (5-in-6 theft roll per item on retreat).

Resurrection Ritual: 1000gp; roll d6 ≤ hero Level to return at full Life. Level 6+ heroes are resurrected automatically once the ritual is paid. The app allows this outside-the-dungeon service to use home bank gold.

A body may instead be laid to rest, making the hero permanently lost and freeing the party to choose a new 1st-level hero between adventures.

entries.title: Leaving the Dungeon
entries.summary: Exit with no fallen inside completes the adventure; survivors fully heal.
entries.body:
The rulebook explicitly says killing the Final Boss and moving out of the dungeon ends the adventure. It also warns that you may not repeatedly exit and re-enter just to heal extra Madness.

In this app, using the dungeon exit when every hero inside is accounted for (no fallen bodies left in the dungeon and no body awaiting recovery outside) is treated as a clean completion.

Surviving heroes fully heal between adventures and keep treasure already on their sheets.

Recovery camps are an exception: if anyone remains fallen inside or a body is awaiting resurrection outside, the party camps outside instead (see Camp Outside).

entries.title: Regroup Party (Camp / Saved)
entries.summary: While camped or from a saved game, swap heroes before re-entering.
entries.body:
The rulebook allows rescue situations and does not restrict changing companions during a rescue camp.

While camped outside the dungeon, or from a manually saved game, use Regroup Party on the party sheet to assign four heroes and marching order.

New heroes join with current roster stats. Replaced heroes are freed for other duties.

Fallen bodies and gear remain on their map tiles even if that hero leaves the active party.

entries.title: Resurrection
entries.summary: 1000gp and d6 ≤ Level to restore a fallen hero to full Life at the exit.
entries.body:
Deliver a fallen hero's body to the dungeon exit to attempt recovery.

Resurrection costs 1000gp. Roll d6 — on ≤ hero Level, they return at full Life. Level 6+ heroes are resurrected automatically once the ritual is paid.

Failure or refusal leaves options to camp and try again or accept permanent loss.

Permanently lost heroes are removed from the roster.

entries.title: Gnome — Gadgeteer
entries.summary: L+6 gadget points; open locks, disarm traps, smokescreen flee.
entries.body:
Gnomes add +½L Defense, +L Saves vs poison and gases.

L spell slots for one chosen illusionist spell studied daily.

L+6 gadget points per adventure. Spend on mechanical attacks (+L ranged), open locks/disarm traps (+L per point spent), free prisoners, or smokescreen (party flees without parting blows).

+L to disarm traps.

entries.title: Kukla
entries.summary: Living doll; secret compartment; green ring revival; one per party.
entries.body:
Rare — one kukla per party. +1 Attack with light slashing weapons; +½L Defense.

Secret torso compartment (gear, 100gp coins, gems). Green ring revives dead kukla; red ring is poison.

200gp carry limit. Cannot use bandages like flesh heroes. Life: 5+L.

entries.title: Light Gladiator
entries.summary: Two light-weapon attacks; optional parry +1 Defense; counter-strike after explosive Defense.
entries.body:
Light gladiators add +½L Attack with light hand weapons only; +½L Defense.

Two light weapons: two attacks per turn, or forgo one to parry (+1 Defense vs melee).

Once per fight: after explosive Defense vs a foe, add the margin to your next Attack vs that foe.

Free Gladiator expert skill at L3. Life: 5+L.

entries.title: Mushroom Monk
entries.summary: Flurry of blows by Tier; spores debuff minors; immune to fungal poison.
entries.body:
Rare — one per party. +L Attack with unarmed/nunchaku/bo/sai/stars; +½L otherwise; +½L Defense.

Flurry: Tier attacks per turn when unarmed or with monk weapons.

Spores: Tier uses per adventure — −1 Level to living minor foes in area.

Immune to fungal creature poison/sleep. Life: 4+L.

entries.title: Marching Order
entries.summary: Positions #1–#4 affect corridor combat, traps, and who meets wandering monsters.
entries.body:
The party marches in order #1 (front) through #4 (rear). Reorder in exploration between fights.

Corridor combat uses marching order to decide who can melee, who fires missiles, and who enemies target.

Wandering monster ambushes in corridors often strike the rear ranks.

Traps that target a hero use marching order to pick victims.

entries.title: Protection, Blessing, and Escape
entries.summary: Defensive spells and Escape; buffs may precede Reactions in combat.
entries.body:
Protection (wizard/cleric): defensive buff on one hero; not treated as attack immediately (p.146).

Blessing (cleric): removes qualifying conditions; 3 uses per adventure.

Escape (wizard): teleports the party out of a lost fight to the entrance in exploration or when rules allow.

Each cast uses once-per-adventure spell slot tracking unless Rest recovers a slot.

entries.title: Wizard Spellcasting
entries.summary: L+2 slots prepared before delve; once per adventure each; Rest recovers one spent slot.
entries.body:
Wizards have L+2 spell slots. Prepare spells before the adventure; slots refresh between adventures.

Each prepared spell may be cast once per adventure unless recovered by Rest (one slot) or spell-burning from the spellbook.

Basic spells: Fireball, Lightning, Sleep, Blessing, Escape, Protection, and others on the wizard list (see basic_spells_table on the home screen).

Fireball: spellcasting roll (exploding tier die + caster Level) must meet foe Level; minion aim slays max(1, total − minion Level) vermin/minions; single boss/weird aim deals 1 Life. Mummies gain +2 on the Fireball roll. Dragons are immune unless undead.

Lightning: connect roll vs foe Level; 1 vermin/minion slain or 2 Life to a boss/weird on hit.

Sleep: no effect on undead, dragons, artificial/construct/elemental/spirit foes, or foes L11+; the combat log names the immune target.

Exploration: door magic (Fireball, Lightning, Warp Wood), Clues on illusion doors.

Combat: cast from party sheet or combat panel; offensive spells skip Reactions.

entries.title: Cleric Prayers
entries.summary: Healing d6+L three times per adventure; Blessing removes conditions.
entries.body:
Clerics cast prayers without a free hand. Each prayer use takes 1 turn in exploration.

Healing prayer: 3 uses per adventure, heal d6+L Life on self or ally.

Blessing: 3 uses per adventure; removes curses, petrification, and similar conditions when allowed by description.

+½ Level to Attack; +Level vs undead.

entries.title: Druid Spells
entries.summary: 2+L slots; basic druid list; expert spells from quests, Clues, or scrolls.
entries.body:
Druids have 2+L spell slots and add +Level to spellcasting.

Prepare from the basic druid list before adventures. Expert druid spells require quest reward, 3 Clues, XP roll, or destroying an expert scroll.

Some spells are outdoor-only per description.

Animal companion: auto-summon on wilderness entry when the druid spends 1 Food ration (see Druid class entry). Companion fights alongside the party until slain.

entries.title: Illusionist Spells
entries.summary: L+3 illusion slots; distracting lights; mirror image, fog, and servant in combat.
entries.body:
Illusionists have L+3 slots for illusion-list spells only (plus named cross-list illusions).

Distracting lights: 1 turn, spell roll vs foe Level — reduce foe Level by Tier for the fight (not undead/constructs).

Combat illusions: Mirror Image absorbs hits; Fog and Servant have turn-limited effects.

Illusionary knife throw may inflict subdual without penalty.

entries.title: Mirror Image, Fog, and Specters
entries.summary: Illusion buffs absorb hits, obscure foes, or add swarm damage in combat.
entries.body:
Illusionist combat effects tracked in session:

• Mirror Image — absorbs incoming hits until images are depleted.
• Illusionary Fog — obscures targeting for a number of turns.
• Specter Swarm — ongoing damage or pressure per spell description.

Illusionary Servant — extra carry capacity in exploration until dispelled by trap or rule.

entries.title: Carrying Capacity
entries.summary: 200gp coin cap in the dungeon; three extra weapon slots beyond starting class gear; over-limit penalties.
entries.body:
In the dungeon each hero may carry at most 200gp in coins.

Weapon slots: 3 total beyond starting class gear. A two-handed weapon uses 2 slots. Up to 2 shields may be carried.

Starting class equipment does not count toward encumbrance — only extra weapons or shields picked up during the adventure do. A warrior who starts with a hand weapon and shield may swap those freely; a second sword from loot counts.

Over-encumbrance (too much gold or extra gear) applies −1 to Defense and Saves until load is reduced.

Between adventures, roster gold is treated as home bank gold and is uncapped. When a hero enters a dungeon, up to 200gp is carried and the rest stays banked outside.

Illusionary Servant can extend carry capacity until dispelled.

entries.title: Transfer Items and Gold
entries.summary: Move gear between heroes in exploration or on the home roster.
entries.body:
In exploration (non-combat), use Transfer on the party sheet to move items or gold between living heroes.

Respects 200gp coin cap, weapon slots (starting class gear + 3 extra), and shield limits.

Home screen transfer works between roster characters for between-adventure setup, but not while a hero is in an active adventure. Roster inventory is stored gear; roster gold is home-bank gold.

When the active dungeon is camped outside, Transfer can move items or home-bank gold between living party members and available roster heroes who are not locked in another session. The transfer dialog labels each hero's available/home-bank gold.

Use Bank for party carried-gold deposit/withdrawal before re-entering; camp transfer treats party gold as outside funds.

Illusionary Servant extends carry capacity for one hero until dispelled.

entries.title: Bandages
entries.summary: Once per hero per adventure in exploration: +1 Life.
entries.body:
Each hero may use one bandage per adventure during exploration.

A bandage restores 1 Life up to maximum Life.

Bandages do not count as magical healing. Bulwarks and other special classes may have additional restrictions on other healing types.

entries.title: Saving Throws
entries.summary: Roll d6 + Save bonus vs target Level; class and encumbrance modify attempts.
entries.body:
When a rule calls for a Save, roll d6 + Save modifiers and meet or beat the listed Level (trap level, poison level, puzzle level, etc.).

Class bonuses apply (e.g. rogue +L vs traps, wizard +L vs magic, halfling Luck reroll).

Encumbrance from extra gear beyond starting class equipment (or excess gold) applies −1 to Defense and Saves.

Paladins auto-succeed Fear Saves. Paladin prayer can reroll one failed Save per point spent.

entries.title: Attack and Defense
entries.summary: Roll d6 + modifiers; meet or beat foe Level to hit; damage from how much you beat Level.
entries.body:
Attack: roll d6 + Attack modifiers. Meet or exceed the foe's Level to hit.

Exploding dice: on a natural 6, roll again and add (melee and defense; some class limits apply).

Damage: for each full point the attack roll exceeds the foe's Level, inflict 1 Life loss (minimum 1 on a hit). Some abilities double damage.

Defense: roll d6 + Defense modifiers vs the attack roll. Success avoids harm.

Armor and shields add Defense. Weapon type modifiers apply vs certain foes.

entries.title: Missile Combat
entries.summary: Opening volley in rooms; corridors limit missiles to rear rank.
entries.body:
In rooms, heroes with ready missile weapons may fire once in the opening round when initiative allows.

In corridors only ranks #3–#4 may fire missiles each round; ranks #1–#2 fight in melee.

After firing missiles, switching to melee in the same round may impose an unarmed penalty (−2) if no free hand.

Foes with missile attacks follow the same broad phase order as the party.

entries.title: Weapon Type Modifiers
entries.summary: Weapon type vs foe type adjusts Attack; two-handed uses two weapon slots.
entries.body:
The combat engine applies weapon-type modifiers from the combat modifiers table (e.g. slashing vs undead, blunt vs skeletons).

Crushing weapons gain +1 Attack vs skeletons/undead and the combat log calls out that bonus when it applies.

Light weapons: −1 Attack unless class ability says otherwise.

Two-handed weapons occupy two weapon slots in the dungeon.

Set default melee/missile weapons on the party sheet; swap in combat costs 1 turn.

entries.title: Corridor Combat
entries.summary: Only front ranks melee in corridors; rear rank may shoot missiles.
entries.body:
In corridors, only heroes in marching positions #1 and #2 may make melee attacks.

Rear ranks (#3–#4) may fire missiles if equipped (bow, sling).

Foes typically target the front ranks. Wandering ambushes in corridors may strike the rear and surprise the party.

Move archers to the rear before End Combat Round to fire an opening volley.

entries.title: Draw Weapon
entries.summary: Drawing a different melee weapon spends the hero's turn; foes then attack.
entries.body:
During combat, a hero may draw a different melee weapon from inventory instead of attacking.

Drawing uses that hero's action for the round; living foes still attack when you End Combat Round.

Set default weapons on the roster or party sheet before fights to avoid mid-combat swaps.

entries.title: Flee and Withdraw
entries.summary: Fleeing triggers parting attacks; withdrawing through a door grants +1 Defense.
entries.body:
Flee: each foe may make one parting attack against assigned heroes. Survivors escape the fight. Roll d6 after fleeing — on 1, wandering monsters may pursue.

Halfling Luck: spending 1 Luck when fleeing skips parting attacks entirely.

Withdraw: move through an adjacent door; each foe attacks once at +1 Defense for the withdrawing hero (withdraw modifier). The party slams the door and ends combat if any survive.

Paladins have special restrictions on breaking off from holy missions.

entries.title: Morale
entries.summary: Foes check morale when losses mount; failed morale means rout or hesitation.
entries.body:
Foes test morale when their side suffers significant losses or when leaders fall.

Failed morale: foes flee, surrender, or fight at disadvantage per table notes.

Major foes and bosses often have special morale rules.

Minor foes slain in one blow by a single hero may not trigger full morale checks (multi-kill rule).

entries.title: Reactions
entries.summary: Before round 1, roll each foe group's reaction — fight, flee, parley, challenge, or demand bribe.
entries.body:
When combat begins, you may Check Reactions before the first round unless the party attacked immediately or cast an offensive spell.

Each living foe group rolls on its bestiary reaction table (d6).

Outcomes include fight, fight to the death, flee, parley, Capture, Puzzle, Magic Challenge, Trade Information, or bribe (gold and/or weapons). Pay bribe to avoid combat if the table allows. Fight-to-the-death results give foes first strike and suppress later morale flight checks.

The session log adds a short Reaction outcome line explaining whether foes flee, attack first, demand payment, offer a challenge, or enter capture mode.

Mixed groups use category fallback tables when no single bestiary applies. The p.102 Capture rule overlays named Minion tables: a living Minion group that rolls 1 is treated as Capture even if its specific bestiary row would otherwise flee or fight.

If the party surprises foes, reactions may be skipped or resolved in the party's favor. Failed-scout reaction checks use the same special outcome handling for Capture, Puzzle, Magic Challenge, and scout-local Bribes.

entries.title: Capture Reaction
entries.summary: Minion reaction roll of 1: foes try to take captives — attacks are non-lethal; heroes at 0 Life are taken prisoner.
entries.body:
When a Minion reaction roll is 1, foes attempt to take the party captive. This overlays named Minion bestiary tables as well as the generic Minion table. Their attacks are non-lethal; heroes reduced to 0 Life are captured rather than slain. Foes strike first on this reaction.

Capture state:
• The capturing foe type and the tile where capture began are recorded.
• Each captured hero is stripped of gold and carried equipment, then escorted off the combat tile (one escort foe is removed per captive).
• Stripped gold is left as treasure; stripped equipment is held in session state and restored on rescue or ransom.
• Captured heroes appear as 'captive' (greyed) in the party sheet and do not act in combat.

Locating the hideout (Someone Has Been Imprisoned):
• Spend 3 Clues (via Reveal Secret picker or the Find Hideout button in the Capture panel) to generate the captive's hideout.
• A new 2d6×2d6 lair is created adjacent to the current tile, connected by a new passage.
• The hideout is guarded by the same foe type at double their normal count.

Rescuing captives:
• Fight through the hideout — captives are restored to d3 Life and recover stripped equipment when the last guard falls.
• Pay ransom — if foes' reaction allows, pay Level×10gp per captive; captives are freed and recover stripped equipment without combat.
• Angelic True Name rescue also frees captives and restores stripped equipment.

Capture panel buttons: 'Find Hideout (3 Clues)' becomes available once the hideout tile does not yet exist; 'Pay Ransom' appears when the party is at the hideout.

entries.title: Magic Challenge Reaction
entries.summary: A reaction row may present a magical challenge; pass a magic Save for a peaceful result or fail into combat.
entries.body:
Reaction rows with key 'magic_challenge' present a spell puzzle or magical challenge.

The first living hero on the current tile attempts a magical Save against the highest living foe Level. Wizards and elves add their Level as a magic-save class bonus. Super Logic/puzzle bonuses also apply where present.

Success ends the encounter peacefully. Failure starts combat with foes striking first and leaves a pending magical Save reroll for eligible class abilities.

Current indexed named rows include Necromancer magical challenge handling; additional source-specific rows can be added as more tables are extracted.

entries.title: Bribes
entries.summary: Some reaction results demand gold or weapons; pay to avoid combat if allowed.
entries.body:
Reaction tables may demand a bribe in gold, weapons, or both.

Pay Bribe spends the required total from the party (respecting carry limits). Decline and combat proceeds.

Dwarves: parties with two or more dwarves cannot bribe (Miser trait).

Jewelry used as bribe counts dwarven resale bonuses where applicable.

entries.title: Foe Categories
entries.summary: Vermin/minions are minor; weird/boss are major for XP and reactions.
entries.body:
Spawn tables roll enemy categories:

• Vermin and Minions — minor foes; count toward the 10-encounter XP tally.
• Weird and Boss — major foes; grant immediate XP credits and may trigger Final Boss checks.

Mixed groups use per-foe reaction tables where available, or category fallbacks.

entries.title: Poisonous Foes
entries.summary: Some hits inflict lingering poison; repeated Saves until cured or duration ends.
entries.body:
Foes with poison attacks may inflict lingering poison on a failed Save.

When a poisonous foe wounds a hero, the combat log names the poison threat, the target, the Save result, any extra damage, and whether the lingering Poisoned Lx state was applied.

Heroes test Saves each round or exploration step as rules specify until the poison ends or is cured (Blessing, Healing, etc.).

Halflings and classes with poison resistance add their bonuses.

Blade poison on party weapons is separate — applied before combat to your attacks.

entries.title: Subdual Damage
entries.summary: Declare subdual to bring foes alive; −1 Attack unless ignored by class ability.
entries.body:
Subdual attacks aim to capture rather than kill. Apply −1 to Attack rolls unless a class ability ignores it (e.g. illusionist knife throw).

Foes reduced to 0 Life by subdual are knocked out, not slain — required for bring-alive quests.

Bring-head quests require a lethal boss kill instead.

entries.title: Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Two-step rolls: connect vs foe Level, then penetrate vs Level + MR.
entries.body:
Offensive spells against foes with Magic Resistance (MR):

1. Spellcasting roll must meet or beat the foe's Level (connect).
2. If connected, roll again to penetrate — target number is foe Level + MR.

Failed penetration wastes the spell slot for that attempt. Defensive and non-targeted spells may bypass MR per spell description.

Casters add class Level to spellcasting rolls.

entries.title: Major Foes and Level Drop
entries.summary: Major foes use higher levels; slaying one may drop effective level of remaining majors.
entries.body:
Major foes (weird monsters, bosses) use higher Level and Life totals.

When a major foe is reduced to half Life, its effective Level drops once; the app marks this as Eff L in combat labels.

When a major foe is slain, remaining major foes on the tile may drop in effective Level per rulebook table.

Major-foe tally feeds the Final Boss check on later room encounters.

Minions fight in groups; rogues gain Attack bonuses when the party outnumbers minor foes.

entries.title: Troll Regeneration
entries.summary: Trolls regain Life each round unless hurt by fire or acid.
entries.body:
Trolls regenerate lost Life at the end of each foe melee phase unless damaged by fire, acid, lightning, or oil since the last regeneration tick (Expanded Edition p.99).

The app tracks suppression per foe: Fireball and holy water (fire), Lightning / Lightning Strike, **acid vials** (shop or loot), and **splashed lantern oil** (shop, caverns loot, or fungal grottoes) all suppress regen for that round (foe card shows Regen blocked).

Major trolls follow the same broad rule with higher Level and Life totals.

entries.title: Final Boss
entries.summary: d6 + major-foes met on room spawns; triple treasure; extra XP roll when slain.
entries.body:
In rooms (not wandering encounters), roll d6 + number of major foes met this adventure. On 6+, the encounter becomes a Final Boss candidate.

Scout-ahead counts as meeting the room's foes: if a scout reveals a room with a weird monster or boss, the Final Boss check is rolled immediately before the Stealth Save, and the same room does not roll that check again when the main party enters.

Final Bosses grant triple treasure and an extra XP roll when defeated. The combat UI highlights Final Boss foes in the top foe chip strip and foe cards.

After the Final Boss dies, Explore mode shows a prominent completion banner explaining that the dungeon objective is complete, while optional quest work may still be finished before leaving.

Slaying the Final Boss enables clean adventure completion at the dungeon exit.

entries.title: Map Element Placement
entries.summary: New tiles roll d66; engine rotates and truncates to avoid overlap.
entries.body:
Exploring an unexplored exit rolls d66 for the new map element key (11–66 for generated areas; 01–06 for entrance elements).

The engine places the tile adjacent to the exit, rotating exits to connect. If the full footprint would overlap explored space or block open exits, the tile may be truncated.

Walkable masks and exit markers from tile metadata control legal movement and connections.

Paper map mode limits coordinates to a 20×28 grid (p.149).

Structural validation for all catalog tiles is in map_elements_validation_table and GET /api/rules/tiles/validation.

entries.title: Map Element Catalog Validation
entries.summary: All 42 starting and generated map elements pass structural validation (grid, exits, shapes).
entries.body:
The visual Map Element Editor maintains walkable grids, cell-shape masks, and exit markers for keys 01–06 (entrance) and 11–66 (generated dungeon).

The engine validates footprint dimensions, walkable/shape rows, in-bounds exits, and catalog completeness via map_elements_validation_table on the home Rules tables panel, GET /api/rules/tiles/validation, and tools/validate_tiles.py.

Gif artwork and exact rulebook layout for entrance tiles remain an authoring audit task; implementation_status on each tile tracks editor review metadata only.

entries.title: Split Party
entries.summary: Implemented support — leave heroes behind, true scout-ahead, detached wandering checks, remote detached combat rounds, simultaneous mixed fights, and current-tile action scoping.
entries.body:
Expanded Edition (p.105, p.79–80) allows leaving heroes behind to guard bodies or scout ahead, with separate wandering-monster checks for detached groups.

The app tracks detached groups per tile, supports Leave behind / Rejoin / Scout ahead from the party sheet, rolls 1-in-6 wanderers for detached groups when the main party moves, and resolves simultaneous front-rank vs major / rear-rank vs minion rounds when both share a tile.

Scout ahead is a two-step UI flow: click Scout ahead on a living hero, then choose an open exit from either the map door marker menu or the Exits panel. Selecting a scout automatically opens the Exits panel and shows a status prompt; closed door rows and map menus explain that the door must be opened before scouting through it. The scout enters the destination map element alone, immediately reveals any Final Boss check for room major foes, and makes a Stealth Save against the highest living foe level there. Halflings and rogues add +L to Stealth; rangers add +L outdoors or +1/2L indoors.

On success, the scout remains unseen in the destination. On failure, the scout may check the foe Reaction table or fight one required solo round; foes have initiative for that first round and target the scout. Scout Bribes spend only the scout group's carried gold/weapons; the main party cannot pay from another tile. After that round the party can Rush to Scout to join the next combat round, or the scout can flee back toward the previous room. The scout cannot simply re-hide in the same location.

The party sheet separates Group 1 - Main Group from Group 2+ - Detached Group blocks, with each detached block labelled by its map element and reason. A Navigate button on detached group headings makes that group active for movement; detached scout rows also show Navigate back / Wait here controls. The Exits panel and map door markers then show routes from the detached group's tile instead of the main party's tile. The map highlights the active detached group with a distinct tile outline and marker.

When Wandering Monsters threaten a group left behind on another tile, the party sheet shows a Detached combat panel. Each click resolves one remote round for the heroes physically on that tile while the main party stays where it is; if the detached group falls, the monsters remain on that tile for the main party to face later.

Reactions, bribes, Trade Information, puzzle saves, flee/withdraw, spellcasting, common consumables, and class abilities use only heroes physically on the current map element. A detached hero away from the current room is visible on the party sheet but cannot use local actions until the party returns, and does not appear in combat — foe chips, hero chips, tactical room tokens, and combat hero rows show only combatants physically in the fight.

entries.title: Room Content
entries.summary: Entering a new map element rolls 2d6 on the Room Content Table.
entries.body:
When the party enters a newly generated room or corridor, roll 2d6 on the Room Content Table (p.106).

Results include empty rooms, vermin, minions, weird monsters, traps, special events, and treasure hoards.

Corridors use the corridor column where the table differs.

Living foes from this roll start combat immediately unless reactions or surprise rules apply.

entries.title: Backtracking
entries.summary: Moving to a visited tile may trigger a wandering-monster roll.
entries.body:
When the party moves to an already explored map element via a known connection, that is backtracking.

Roll d6 for wandering monsters on a 1 or 2 (see Wandering Monsters Table).

If wanderers spawn, they appear on the destination tile. Living foes there must be fought before resting or leaving.

Open doors and passages stay open when returning through them.

entries.title: Searching
entries.summary: Once per map element: roll d6 (corridors −1); on 5–6 choose one reward.
entries.body:
Search is attempted once per map element. Roll d6; in corridors subtract 1 from the roll.

On 5–6, the party finds something. After the successful roll, choose one reward:

• Hidden Treasure — gold or items using the Hidden Treasure rules.
• Secret Door — may reveal a new exit on this tile.
• Secret Passage — may shift the environment to caverns or fungal grottoes (EE p.112–113).
• Clue — choose the character who holds 1 Clue for puzzles, illusion doors, spells, trade information, and some quests.

Held Clues are spent deliberately after they are found. The Search Clue button gains a new character-held Clue; it does not spend held Clues.

entries.title: Clues
entries.summary: Gain Clues from Search; persistent character-held Clues can be traded or spent deliberately.
entries.body:
A successful Search reward choice can add 1 Clue to a selected character. Rulebook Clues accumulate across adventures; the app stores them on individual roster characters and restores the party total from those holders in the next dungeon. Legacy saves with pooled Clues are migrated to the first living character.

Uses:
• Reveal Secret — spend 3 Clues to reveal a selected Expanded Edition p.123 Secret; choose the PC who discovers it. Location of a Hidden Treasure is wired for an empty non-entrance room; Location of a Magic Item rolls magic treasure for the current room; Location of a Scroll grants a basic spell scroll; Weakness of a Foe gives +2 party Attack vs one chosen Major Foe for that combat; Deal with a Foe ends eligible non-vermin/non-Final-Boss encounters without treasure or XP; True Name of a Spiritual Entity offers angelic rescue/healing or demonic foe damage; New Spell adds a selected spell and one temporary slot for this adventure; Increase of Magical or Spiritual Power adds one permanent use of a selected spell/prayer; Your Enemy Is in the Dungeon swaps a Major Foe for a Chaos Champion and gives +1 Attack against it; The Prisoner adds an NPC rescue reward to a guarded room; Terrifying Secret forces the next eligible vermin/minion morale test to fail; Secret Diet spends 1 Food ration while camped outside for +1 Life this adventure; Bloodline of Dragon-Slayers is +1 Attack/Defense vs dragons; Recipe for a Potion validates 2 defeated Major Foes and 50gp components, then unlocks the 50gp Potion of Healing price in the equipment shop; Someone Will Pay Big Money for That triples one gem/jewel/jewelry sale and is consumed. Future-use Secrets show timing prompts on sheets, encounter-start hints in the log, and combat status reminders when the timing window opens.
• Someone Has Been Imprisoned (capture secret) — spend 3 Clues when a hero is held captive by foes to locate the captive hideout. A new 2d6×2d6 lair is generated adjacent to the current tile, guarded by the same foe type at double count. Captives are found there with d3 Life. Pay Level×10gp ransom instead of fighting if the foes' reaction allows. Available via the Reveal Secret picker (requires active captives) or the Find Hideout button in the Capture panel.
• Trade Information — on the p.102 reaction, gain 25gp per Clue held by heroes physically in the encounter without losing those Clues, and/or buy 1 Clue for 100gp using gold carried by heroes physically in the encounter.
• Spell learning — eligible wizard/elf expert spell learning may spend 3 Clues; Expert-trained L5+ druids may spend 3 Clues to learn an unlearned spell from the druid spell table.
• Illusion doors — spend 3 Clues instead of an illusionist spellcasting roll.
• Lever doors — spend 1 Clue or use a gnome gadget.
• Some quests and special discoveries (e.g. Kerrak Dar hoard: 1 Clue while Searching).

The app does not auto-convert every 3 Clues into a Secret/XP result; the player chooses the spend. Spending drains the selected/acting character's Clues first, then other holders if needed. Discovered Secrets appear on the home and active party sheets.

entries.title: Hidden Treasure
entries.summary: Search finds loot by formula; some hoards trigger alarms or traps.
entries.body:
When Search finds hidden treasure, roll gold and items using the Hidden Treasure Table (p.108).

Some results are protected by traps or alarms. An alarm may spawn wandering monsters before the party can claim the hoard.

Treasure already rolled on room entry (Treasure Table) is separate from hidden search results.

entries.title: Door Magic (Exploration)
entries.summary: Cast Fireball, Lightning, or Warp Wood on eligible doors outside combat.
entries.body:
In exploration, wizards (and others with slots) may cast door-targeting spells from the party sheet or exit panel:

• **Fireball / Lightning** — destroy iron doors when no foes remain in the room; shatter sealed doors per Door Table notes.
• **Warp Wood** — may ruin wooden doors or barriers.

Each spell cast consumes its once-per-adventure slot unless recovered by Rest.

Offensive door magic in combat follows normal combat spell rules.

entries.title: Iron, Sealed, Illusion, and Lever Doors
entries.summary: Some door results need spells, Clues, or class abilities instead of a simple open roll.
entries.body:
Door Table results beyond stuck/locked/trapped include:

• **Iron** — cannot be bashed; Rogue lock-pick or Fireball/Lightning only. Exits panel shows “no bash” and highlights spell destroy buttons when the party has no Rogue.
• **Sealed** — magical seal; spellcasting roll vs door level (once).
• **Illusion** — spend 3 character-held Clues or illusionist spellcasting roll.
• **Lever** — spend 1 character-held Clue or gnome gadget.

Unexplored doors show a hint that the first attempt rolls 2d6; warriors/barbarians get a Bash/roll-door action if the result is locked.

Fireball/Lightning on iron doors with no foes in the room destroys the door directly (no misleading “no targets” log).

entries.title: Lockpick and Bash
entries.summary: Locked doors require a rogue lockpick or warrior/barbarian bash attempt.
entries.body:
Locked doors cannot be opened by simply trying the handle.

• Rogues add +Level to lockpick attempts and always may try.
• Warriors and barbarians may bash instead of pick.
• Other classes need magic, spells, or special tools unless the table says otherwise.

Encumbrance penalizes door attempts. Failed attempts may still trigger trapped doors.

entries.title: Opening Doors
entries.summary: Unexplored doors roll 2d6 on the Door Table; open doors stay synced both ways.
entries.body:
Closed doors must be opened before moving through. Roll 2d6 on the Door Table (p.109):

• Unlocked — opens easily.
• Stuck — Strength Save vs door level.
• Locked — Rogue lockpick or Warrior/Barbarian bash; encumbrance penalizes attempts.
• Trapped — triggers the Trap Table when opened or crossed.
• Iron, sealed, illusion, lever — special handling; spells, Clues, Fireball/Lightning, or Warp Wood may help in exploration.

Once a door is open, the linked exit on the other tile shows the same state.

Entrance threshold doors into the dungeon open without a roll the first time you explore through them (p.25). The outside dungeon exit starts open.

entries.title: Strength Saves
entries.summary: Stuck doors require a Strength Save vs door level.
entries.body:
Door Table results of Stuck require a Strength Save against the door's level.

Warriors and barbarians may bash stuck or locked doors instead of picking.

Encumbrance applies −1 to physical Saves including door attempts.

entries.title: Blade Poison
entries.summary: Apply poison to a weapon before combat; failed Saves inflict extra harm.
entries.body:
Blade poison is purchased from the wandering alchemist or found as loot.

Apply to a weapon before combat begins. On a successful hit, the foe Saves vs poison or suffers additional effects per table.

Poisonous foes may inflict lingering poison on heroes — repeated Saves until cured or duration ends.

entries.title: Holy Water
entries.summary: Throw at undead in combat or exploration; area effect per rulebook.
entries.body:
Holy water harms undead on a successful use. Throw in combat as an action or use in exploration when rules allow.

Barbarians may buy and use holy water despite not using other magic items.

entries.title: Illusion and Lever Doors
entries.summary: Spend held Clues or use door magic on special doors.
entries.body:
Illusion doors hide true exits until dispelled or bypassed with Clues, Fireball, Lightning, or Warp Wood.

Lever doors need the correct lever sequence — Clues from Search help.

Held Clues are owned by individual characters and spent deliberately; the Search Clue button gains a new character-held Clue, it does not spend them.

entries.title: Potions
entries.summary: Potion of Healing restores all lost Life once per hero per adventure.
entries.body:
Potion of Healing: restore all lost Life. Once per hero per adventure; usable even during combat as a free action.

Barbarians cannot use potions — they may carry potions for allies.

Buy from wandering alchemist or home equipment shop when available. Recipe for a Potion unlocks the 50gp equipment-shop price after its Secret prerequisites/payment are resolved.

entries.title: Scrolls
entries.summary: Burn to cast once; wizards may copy unknown spells into a spellbook (destroys scroll).
entries.body:
Any hero allowed scroll use may burn a scroll to cast the spell once (as L1 caster unless class says otherwise).

Wizards add +Level to scroll casting rolls.

Wizards may copy an unknown spell from a scroll into the spellbook — the scroll is destroyed. Copied spells become part of future preparation.

Barbarians cannot use scrolls.

entries.title: Charged Wands and Staves
entries.summary: Use charged wands and staves from inventory; each cast spends 1 charge without using a memorized slot.
entries.body:
Magical treasure may grant charged items such as Wand of Sleep (3 charges) or Fireball Staff (2 charges).

During combat or exploration, use the item button on the hero's party sheet. The spell resolves like a scroll cast (+Level for wizards, elves, druids, clerics, and illusionists) but does not consume a prepared spell slot.

Each use spends 1 charge. The inventory entry updates to show remaining charges; the item is removed when spent.

Offensive casts from magic items skip Reactions the same way as memorized offensive spells.

Barbarians cannot use magic items (may carry for allies).

entries.title: Caverns and Fungal Grottoes
entries.summary: Secret passage search can shift tables to cavern or fungal variants.
entries.body:
The party normally delves in the dungeon environment. Finding a secret passage via Search may move the party into caverns or fungal grottoes (EE p.112–113).

Each environment routes trap, treasure, special-event, and wandering tables to its variant where applicable.

Paper map mode limits placement to a 20×28 grid (p.149).

entries.title: Bags of Nails
entries.summary: 4gp each; one bag nails one door shut when resting.
entries.body:
Bag of nails costs 4gp from the equipment shop.

When Resting, spend one bag per door to nail shut. Nailed doors give warning if wanderers arrive during rest (party may strike first).

Rest without nailing lets wanderers surprise the party.

Only doors qualify — cavern openings cannot be nailed.

entries.title: Resting
entries.summary: Once per adventure in a cleared room with adjacent cleared tiles and nailable doors.
entries.body:
The party may rest once per adventure when all of the following are true:

• The party is in a cleared room (no living foes on the tile).
• Every adjacent explored room or corridor is also cleared.
• The room has doors that can be nailed shut (cavern openings do not qualify).

Each hero chooses to recover 1 Life or recover one spent ability (spell slot, Healing prayer use, rage attack, Luck point, or paladin prayer point). Heroes at full Life with nothing to recover gain nothing from a Life choice.

The party may nail doors shut using one bag of nails per door (4gp each). Nailed doors give warning on a wandering-monster roll (party may attack first). Unnailed doors let wanderers surprise the party.

After resting, roll d6 for wandering monsters on a 1.

Halflings may cook a Nourishing Meal once per adventure when resting: spend 1 Food ration per ally eating. Each eater heals +1 Life (in addition to rest recovery). Halflings also recover 1 Madness.

entries.title: Wandering Monsters
entries.summary: Roll d6 on 1 after rest, flee, noise events, or backtrack — category from table.
entries.body:
Wandering monsters use the Wandering Monsters Table.

Common triggers:
• After resting — d6 on 1.
• After fleeing combat — d6 on 1 may pursue.
• Backtrack movement — d6 on 1 or 2 (see table).
• Special events and alarms.

Nailed doors during rest give the party warning (party may attack first). Unnailed doors let wanderers surprise the party.

Corridor ambushes may target the rear guard and act before the party in round 1.

entries.title: Campaign Modes
entries.summary: Four campaign modes: Classical rolls, Slow and Sure completion, Old School tally, Slower Advancement bank.
entries.body:
Choose at adventure start (Campaign mode):

• Classical — earn XP rolls from minors, majors, secrets, and bosses; spend to advance mid-adventure.
• Slow and Sure — +1 Level for each hero who completes the adventure alive.
• Old School — tally XP from defeated foes and treasure; spend (Tier+2)×100 to level or buy a skill.
• Slower Advancement — bank XP like Classical, then spend Level XP (+ optional extra for +1) before rolling to advance.

Basic tier: advancement roll d6 > Level (6 always succeeds).
Expert-trained heroes: advancement roll d8+2 > Level or natural 7–8 on the d8. Expert-trained L5+ heroes may learn expert skills/spells instead of gaining a level.

Expert tier entry is a separate Tier training cost (500gp or 1 banked XP roll) and is required before Level 6, Expert dice, or Expert skill/spell learning.

Mid-adventure level-up: +1 Life and max Life, immediate class benefits, casters gain spell slots with in-session spell picker.

entries.title: Classical XP Rolls
entries.summary: Basic heroes roll d6 > Level; Expert-trained heroes roll d8+2 and may learn Expert skills instead of leveling.
entries.body:
Classical campaign mode: eligible heroes spend earned XP rolls mid-adventure.

Basic heroes roll d6 > current Level (6 always succeeds).
Expert-trained heroes roll d8+2 > current Level OR natural 7–8 on the d8 (Four Against the Abyss).

Expert-trained L5+ heroes may learn an expert skill/spell instead of gaining a level. Expert tier entry itself is separate: pay 500gp or 1 banked XP roll through Tier training first.

Spend pending rolls from the party sheet when ready. Same hero cannot level twice in one adventure.

Major foes and Final Boss grant extra rolls. Old School and Slower Advancement use tallies or banked XP instead.

entries.title: Old School and Slower Advancement
entries.summary: Bank XP from defeated foes; spend thresholds to level between adventures.
entries.body:
Old School XP: tally points from defeated enemies during the adventure. Between adventures, spend accumulated XP to buy levels per the Old School cost table.

Slower Advancement: similar bank with higher costs for a grittier campaign.

Slow and Sure: skip mid-adventure rolls — each survivor gains +1 Level when the adventure completes cleanly.

Choose the system when starting a session; it persists for that save.

entries.title: Level Advancement
entries.summary: Tier advancement roll mid-adventure; +Life, class perks, caster spell growth; Expert-trained heroes may learn Expert skills instead.
entries.body:
When an advancement roll succeeds during an adventure:

• Level up: +1 Life and +1 maximum Life (class Life offset applies).
• Class combat bonuses update immediately (+1/2 Level steps for half-level classes).
• Wizards gain L+2 total slots; elves L; druids 2+L; illusionists L+3 — pick new spells in session.
• Clerics gain improved Healing prayer (d6+L).

Basic tier uses d6. Trained higher tiers use the Forsaken Depths summary table (Expert d8+2, Heroic d10+4, Legendary d12+8, Epic d20+10).

After Expert tier training, Classical mode offers a fork on the party sheet: Level up or Learn expert skill/spell instead. Expert tier entry costs 500gp or 1 banked XP roll and is paid separately from the later skill-learning XP roll.

The same hero may not level twice in one adventure unless rules explicitly allow.

entries.title: Minor Encounter XP
entries.summary: Classical XP: one credit after every 10 minor-foe victories.
entries.body:
Under the Classical XP system, defeating vermin and minions (minor categories) counts toward a running tally.

Every 10 minor encounters cleared grants one XP roll credit for the party.

Major foes (weird, boss) grant immediate XP credits instead.

Progress persists on character records when you save, camp, or complete an adventure.

entries.title: Slow and Sure XP
entries.summary: +1 Level for each survivor who completes the adventure alive.
entries.body:
Choose Slow and Sure at adventure start.

When the party leaves the dungeon successfully, each surviving hero gains 1 Level automatically.

No d6 XP roll is required. Spell pickers appear if casters gain new slots.

entries.title: Attack Immediately vs Reactions
entries.summary: Skip Reaction roll only when charging in; offensive spells also skip Reactions.
entries.body:
At the start of combat you may Check Reactions or attack immediately.

Attack immediately: skip the Reaction roll and fight; eligible missile shots fire first in rooms.

Offensive spells (Fireball, Lightning, Sleep, etc.) cast at combat start also skip Reactions per p.146.

Defensive buffs (Protection, Barkskin, Illusionary Armor) do not count as attacking immediately — you may still Check Reactions first.

Surprised parties cannot attack first; foes act in round 0.

entries.title: Combat Initiative
entries.summary: Opening round order depends on surprise; corridors restrict who fights and who is hit.
entries.body:
Room combat: if the party is surprised or attacked immediately, eligible heroes with missile weapons fire once before melee. Otherwise party and foes alternate by phase.

Corridor combat: rear rank (#3–#4) fires missiles; front rank (#1–#2) melees; foes attack the front rank. Wandering ambushes in corridors hit the rear guard.

Surprised party: foes act first in the opening round.

Each combat round: party missiles (if allowed) → foe missiles/gaze → party melee → foe melee.

Offensive spells skip the optional Reaction roll (p.146). Defensive buffs may be cast before Check Reactions.

entries.title: Starting Combat
entries.summary: Room encounters wait for Start Combat; use Exits to leave without fighting.
entries.body:
When you enter a room with foes, combat does not begin until you choose Start Combat (wandering monsters and statue ambushes attack immediately).

While foes are present in exploration, use Exits to leave the room without fighting, or Start Combat when ready (p.146). The session UI shows a brief encounter hint listing foes on the tile.

After starting: Check Reactions (d6 on foe table) in the sticky action bar, Withdraw through a door in round 0, or Fight Round / an offensive spell to attack immediately.

The combat panel shows phase steps, foe cards, hero target/ability rows, round plan summary, and expected foe attacks. A top foe chip strip mirrors the bottom party chips: major foes are shown individually, identical vermin/minions are grouped, Final Boss chips are visually distinct, and hover/click details show traits such as undead, poison, MR, regeneration, and multiple attacks. Spells, potions, and class buttons remain on party sheets below.

Offensive spells cast at combat start skip Reactions. Defensive buffs do not.

Fight Round resolves the whole round — party attacks, then living foes.

entries.title: Surprise
entries.summary: Surprised parties cannot attack first; corridor wanderers may ambush the rear.
entries.body:
Some encounters surprise the party (wandering corridor ambush, certain events).

A surprised party cannot attack immediately in round 0 — Check Reactions or End Combat Round still applies, but foes may strike first.

Nailed doors during rest give warning so the party may attack first on a wandering roll.

Unnailed doors let wanderers surprise the party.

entries.title: Paper Map Mode
entries.summary: Optional 20×28 placement limit at session start (EE p.149).
entries.body:
When starting a session, choose Paper map mode to limit placement to a 20×28 grid.

Unlimited mode (default) uses a larger grid.

If no legal placement exists after truncation, the exit remains unexplored.

entries.title: Lady in White
entries.summary: Quest offer on eligible tiles; accept to track an Ongoing Quest.
entries.body:
The Lady in White may appear on map elements flagged by special content.

Accepting starts an Ongoing Quest tracked in the session panel with map markers.

Progress by reaching objectives, subduing or slaying targets, or returning items as the Quest Table specifies.

Claim Epic Rewards when the quest completes.

entries.title: Quests
entries.summary: Quest Table offers missions; subdue for bring-alive; Epic Rewards on claim.
entries.body:
Accept quests from the Lady in White or Quest Table events.

Track progress in Ongoing Quests. Map markers show quest locations.

Bring-alive objectives require subdual, not killing.

Bring-head objectives require slaying the target.

Epic Rewards on claim may include expert spells, gear, or bonuses instead of standard treasure.

entries.title: Epic Rewards
entries.summary: Completing quests may grant Epic Rewards instead of standard treasure.
entries.body:
When a quest's objectives are met, Claim Reward on the Ongoing Quests panel.

Epic Rewards may include expert spells (druid), magic items, gold, or campaign bonuses per Quest Table row.

Bring-alive objectives require subdual; bring-head requires a lethal boss kill.

Some rewards persist to the character roster on clean dungeon exit.

entries.title: Special Events
entries.summary: Room content and tables can spawn ghosts, merchants, quests, and environment events.
entries.body:
Special events come from room content rolls and dedicated special-event tables.

Examples in play:
• Ghost — interaction or combat per table.
• Wandering healer — once per adventure reroll on this tile.
• Wandering alchemist — buy potions or blade poison.
• Lady in White — may offer a quest.

Event and feature table results log visible Event/Feature lines even in Summary mode. Effects that change a hero state or deal damage, such as ghost fear, rockfall, puzzle boxes, curses, healing, poison, or blessings, log targeted Effect lines naming the affected hero.

Ghost events log immunity, saves, failed fear saves, and Life loss per hero. Repeat healer, alchemist, and refused Lady in White events log the substitution reason and route into the existing wandering-monster combat or Resolve Trap flow.

Statue and puzzle-box special features use explicit table choices: leave/touch the statue, or leave/attempt the puzzle box. Failed puzzle-box attempts deal 1 Life damage and leave the box available for another attempt.

Caverns and fungal grottoes use their own special-event table variants.

entries.title: Wandering Alchemist
entries.summary: Buy potions or blade poison when the alchemist special event appears.
entries.body:
The Wandering Alchemist sells Potion of Healing and blade poison during exploration when the event tile is active.

Purchases spend party gold from the buying hero's carried wealth (200gp dungeon cap).

Potions follow once-per-hero-per-adventure use rules. Blade poison is applied before a fight begins.

entries.title: Wandering Healer
entries.summary: Special event: once per adventure reroll on this tile for healing.
entries.body:
The Wandering Healer special event offers limited healing when encountered on a map element.

Each party may benefit once per adventure from the healer's reroll on that tile.

Treat as a special-event result from room content or the Special Events Table, not a guaranteed spawn.

entries.title: Claim Treasure
entries.summary: Split gold evenly among survivors; resolve traps before claiming protected hoards.
entries.body:
Claim Treasure on a cleared tile with a hoard divides gold evenly among living heroes (200gp carry cap each). If a hero is at the cap, their uncarried share is redistributed to living heroes with capacity; the log names capped heroes and the final payouts.

Items are assigned to carriers automatically where possible, and the log names each recipient.

Traps protecting treasure must be resolved first. Alarm traps may spawn wanderers before claim.

Empty treasure rolls remove the map marker.

entries.title: Treasure Rolls
entries.summary: Room entry rolls d6 on Treasure Table; claim splits gold among survivors.
entries.body:
Many rooms roll treasure when first entered (d6 on Treasure Table, p.157).

Empty hoards clear the treasure marker on the map.

Claim Treasure splits gold evenly among living heroes (respecting 200gp carry each), redistributes capped shares to heroes with capacity, and logs any +0gp capped heroes. Items are assigned with recipient names in the log.

Environment variants (caverns, fungal) use their treasure sub-tables where noted.

entries.title: Magical Treasure
entries.summary: Treasure roll of 6 or magical table entries grant scrolls, potions, wands, or staves.
entries.body:
Magical treasure uses the Magical Treasure Table (p.158) and environment variants.

Results may include potions, scrolls, charged wands and staves, or special components.

Use charged wands/staves from the party sheet; each cast spends 1 charge without using a memorized slot.

Generic magic weapon entries roll d6 for weapon type at award (p.163).

entries.title: Magic Weapons
entries.summary: +1 Attack when wielded as default; class and magic restrictions apply.
entries.body:
Magic weapons from treasure grant +1 Attack when set as the hero's default wielded weapon.

Roll d6 when a generic magic weapon is found to determine weapon type.

Class restrictions and magic-use limits still apply for wielding/using the weapon, but treasure pickup may assign the weapon to any legal carrier with capacity when no current hero can wield it.

Resale: 100gp + 2× base weapon cost (p.19).

entries.title: Traps
entries.summary: Trapped exits roll on the Trap Table; rogues may attempt to disarm.
entries.body:
When the party finds a Trap, roll on the Trap Table (p.164) to determine its nature.

Environment variants use caverns (p.165) or fungal grottoes (p.166) tables when applicable.

A living rogue in marching-order position 1 or 2 may attempt to detect and disarm the trap before it goes off. If the disarm attempt fails, the trap triggers and the rogue still gets any Save allowed by the trap description.

Treasure protected by traps must be disarmed or resolved before claiming loot.

entries.title: Expert Skill Combat Actions
entries.summary: Declare round combat skills from the hero drawer; multi-target picks for Double Attack, Double Kick, Protective Incense.
entries.body:
Combat-round expert skills are chosen from each hero's Target/Ability rows in the Combat Focus hero drawer (or the legacy combat panel sidebar) before Fight Round:

• Whirlwind of Steel — once per encounter, chain up to two extra minion attacks at −1/−2 after a minion kill (no exploding dice).
• Double Attack — pick a primary and secondary foe before resolving.
• Deadly Strike, Protective Incense — Protective Incense asks which ally receives the Defense bonus.
• Double Kick (acrobat) — choose up to two minor foes when declaring the trick.
• Knife Throwing — ranged light slashing weapon at −1; weapon returns after the fight.
• Continual Light — cleric forfeit melee attacks to maintain a light source.
• Turn Undead — once per encounter, affects all undead in combat; roll d6+½L vs each undead foe's Level, causing d6 Life loss on each success.

Reactive skills:
• Shield Bash — after an exploding Defense with a shield, free attack at −1 vs that foe (once per encounter).
• Dying Action — when reduced to 0 Life, one Attack at +1 before falling (once per encounter).
