Combat Acrobatics swaps marching order (full turn, no attack). Turn Undead and sleep spores use party-sheet or hero-drawer buttons with hover text for eligibility/spent-use states.

Expert spells with extra targets: Infallible Missile (L8+) may pick a second foe; Phantasmal Binding and Water Jet use foe target rows.

entries.title: Combat Panel (Session UI)
entries.summary: Legacy sidebar combat panel when Combat Focus is off; spells and consumables also on party sheets.
entries.body:
When Combat Focus layout is inactive, the side panel shows a dedicated Combat section:

• Phase steps — Reactions, Plan round (or Bribe), Resolve.
• Foe cards — Life, level, tags, regen/poison/MR chips.
• Context notes — summoned beast, druid companion Life, corridor/ambush hints.
• Hero rows — marching order, plan label, Target and Ability selects (Bulwark Guard when sacrificing).
• Round plan — summary of each hero's target and declared ability before Fight Round.
• Expected foe attacks — preview of who each foe will strike (after reactions resolve).

During combat or a pending encounter, **Combat Focus** is the default layout (tactical map, command rail, hero drawer). See the Combat Focus reference entry.

Fight Round resolves the round and appends a one-line **Round summary** to the log. The summary names who damaged whom, which foe was killed by which hit when inferable, which hero took damage, regeneration blocks, or a clear no-event round.

Fight Round, Flee, Flee (Luck), and Withdraw buttons live here or on the slim combat deck. Withdraw offers a door picker when multiple exits exist.

Spells (with foe/ally targeting, Lifeforce amount, Mass Teleport allies/destination), potions, holy water, lantern oil, acid vials, and class ability buttons stay on expanded party sheets and the Combat Focus hero drawer.

entries.title: Map Exits Overlay
entries.summary: Collapsible Exits dock on the play map lists each exit with travel and door shortcuts.
entries.body:
The Exits overlay lists every **reachable** exit on the current room — only passages on visible, walkable map edges (same markers as the play map). Hidden or invalid exit rows are omitted.

Each row shows direction/kind and offers Travel or door shortcuts (Lock-pick, Bash, Open, Spellcast, Spend clues) with a hero dropdown when several characters can act.

**Iron doors:** status shows “no bash”; without a Rogue, Fireball/Lightning buttons are highlighted and sorted first.

**Unrolled doors:** note that the first attempt rolls 2d6; warriors see Bash/roll-door labels.

Long exit lists scroll inside the dock with a sticky scroll hint. Open/closed state persists in layout preferences.

entries.title: Session Map Layout
entries.summary: Play map zoom/pan, room panel, icon key, room-state markers, class icons, resizable splits, and saved layout prefs.
entries.body:
The session map supports viewport zoom and pan with overlays pinned to the viewport.

Collapsible panels: room details (top-right), Exits dock (bottom-right), icon key (bottom-left).

Room-state markers distinguish live foes, defeated foes, searched rooms, full/claimed/empty treasure, active/resolved traps, fallen heroes, detached heroes, active detached navigation groups, vendors, events, and quest givers. The current-party marker includes class icons for living party members.

During pending encounters and combat, a compact foe chip strip sits above the map/tactical stage while party chips sit below. Foe chips are color-coded by category, group identical minor foes, and make Final Boss status prominent.

Door and passage markers open the same navigation actions as the Exits panel, including scout-through when a scout is selected and detached-group movement when a detached group is active.

Draggable resizers adjust log height, map stage height, and side-panel width (double-click resets). Layout preferences persist in browser localStorage.

Paper map mode (optional 20×28 grid) blocks placement outside bounds at session start.

entries.title: Icon Registry and Map Markers
entries.summary: Rules tables and Icon Editor expose generated defaults plus icons.json overrides for map, class, and monster icons.
entries.body:
GET /api/rules/icons merges custom icons.json rows with generated defaults for room states, every playable class, monster categories, and each named monster.

The Home Rules tables panel lists those icon definitions under Icon registry (generated defaults + icons.json). The Icon Editor can assign user SVG/PNG/WebP files to any generated or custom row.

Unassigned icon rows use built-in CSS fallback glyphs. Existing icons.json entries override generated defaults, so committed custom art keeps priority.

The play map uses these definitions for room-state markers and the Icon Key. A single-monster-type room can use a monster-specific id such as monster-goblins; mixed groups fall back to the generic monster marker. A special event that resolves as wandering monsters uses the wandering-monsters marker instead of the generic event marker.

entries.title: Adventure Lock (One Session Per Hero)
entries.summary: Heroes in an active dungeon session cannot join another until it completes or is deleted.
entries.body:
When a hero is assigned to an in-progress session, their roster entry shows they are gone adventuring and cannot be added to another party or start a duplicate session.

The lock clears when the session completes (clean exit) or is deleted from In Progress / Saved Games.

Camp outside and saved games keep the session open — regroup can swap heroes while the delve persists.

entries.title: Held Foes (Phantasmal Binding)
entries.summary: Held foes skip actions; attacks against them gain +2 and may subdue.
entries.body:
Phantasmal Binding and similar effects add a Held tag to a foe.

Held foes cannot act on their turn. Attacks against held targets gain +2 to hit and may apply subdual damage when subdual mode is active.

The combat UI shows held/poison/MR status on foe cards.

entries.title: Combat Focus (Tactical Layout)
entries.summary: Default combat layout: tactical room view, command rail (Exits/Encounter/Log), hero drawer, slim action deck.
entries.body:
When combat starts or foes are present on the tile, the session switches to **Combat Focus**:

• **Tactical map** — room-centric view with hero tokens and foe markers; optional **Cinema view** hides chrome for a larger map.
• **Foe chips** — top strip mirrors the party chips, groups identical minor foes, highlights Final Bosses, and exposes foe traits/tags/statuses on hover or click, including undead, poison, MR, caster, dragon, construct, regeneration, attacks, bloodied, subdued, and Final Boss.
• **Command rail** — Exits (travel/withdraw), Encounter (foe summary), and Log (Summary keeps outcome summaries and state/effect changes while Verbose shows rolls, table lookups, and math). When no higher-priority reaction/bribe/trade prompt is active, the status line summarizes active foe specials such as poison saves, MR tiers, regeneration, construct immunities, and multiple attacks. The encounter preview expands those live specials into short rules reminders, and expected foe attacks group multi-attack foes into one row with their target list and attack count.
• **Hero chips & drawer** — click a hero to open targeting, Ability picks (expert tricks + heroic Aggressive/Defensive Stance, Master Strike), class tricks, spells, potions, Halfling Luck rerolls, and status hover text such as Shield or +1 vs undead/demons without scrolling the main panel.
• **Slim combat deck** — primary round actions (Fight Round, flee, withdraw, reactions) stay on one row.

Multi-target planning (Double Attack second foe, Double Kick minors, Protective Incense ally, Infallible Missile L8+ second target) is declared in the hero drawer before Fight Round.

Layout fits one viewport on typical screens; exploration mode uses the standard session map layout.

entries.title: Class Tricks and Abilities (Tiers 2–4)
entries.summary: Tier 1–4 class tricks wired per home table; heroic/legendary 45/45 + 20/20 fully wired.
entries.body:
**Tier 1 (L1–4)** — rage, Luck, Panache, paladin prayer: fully wired. Paladin healing uses an explicit target selector on the party sheet.

**Tier 2 (wired):** acrobat tricks including Knife Throw; assassin hide; illusionist distract, Continual Light, Illusionary Knife Throw; gnome smokescreen/gadget/door/trap/free prisoner; mushroom spores; light gladiator dual wield/parry/counter; paladin steed (+1 mounted outdoors); swashbuckler dual wield + Panache. Targeted tricks show ally/foe selectors where needed.

**Tier 3–4 (wired):** Graceful Move, Hyphae (Search/Clue/secret door/passage), kukla prehensile hair lockpick + Army of Dolls, bulwark Sacrifice Defense/Shield + Limited healing, Divine Smite.

See **class_tricks_implementation_table** on the home Rules tables panel. The table describes targeted controls such as Combat Acrobatics ally swap, Lesser Necromancy fallen-hero target, and kukla ring/compartment choices.

**Kukla rings and compartment:** wired. Green ring revives a selected fallen kukla, red ring poison targets a selected foe, and the torso compartment can stash/retrieve items or gold.

**Heroic & Legendary:** **45/45 heroic** and **20/20 legendary** wired.
